rĕ-mălĕdīco , ĕre, v. n.,
I.to return reproachful language, to abuse or revile back: non oportere maledici senatoribus, remaledici civile fasque esse, Vespas. ap. Suet. Vesp. 9 fin.; Tert. Idol. 21; Hier. Ep. 69, 9.
From A Latin Dictionary (Charlton T. Lewis, Charles Short, Oxford, Clarendon Press, 1879)
